subject: chemistry
title: Energetics & Thermochemistry Adventure 2: Hess's law and bond enthalpies
welcome_lead: Today you'll use Hess's law to find unmeasurable ΔH values.
meta_desc: Chemistry — Hess's law, energy cycles, bond enthalpy, mean bond enthalpy.
final_note: You learned Hess's law states ΔH depends only on initial and final states, and bond enthalpies estimate ΔH via bonds broken minus bonds made.

concepts.def: Energy to break 1 mol of bonds (g)

walkthroughs.body_html:
'The enthalpy change is independent of route.'

If A → B = +50 kJ via one path, it's +50 kJ via any other.

This works because H is a state function.

Construct cycles linking unknown ΔH to known ΔH (combustion, formation).

Find ΔH for C(s) + ½O₂(g) → CO(g).

Known: ΔH_c(C) = -394 (C→CO₂); ΔH_c(CO) = -283 (CO→CO₂).

Cycle: C → CO → CO₂, also C → CO₂.
ΔH(C→CO) + ΔH(CO→CO₂) = ΔH(C→CO₂)
ΔH(C→CO) = -394 − (-283) = -111 kJ/mol.

Estimate ΔH:

ΔH ≈ Σ bonds broken − Σ bonds made

For CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(g):
Broken: 4 C-H (412) + 2 O=O (496) = 1648 + 992 = 2640.
Made: 2 C=O (805) + 4 O-H (463) = 1610 + 1852 = 3462.
ΔH = 2640 − 3462 = -822 kJ/mol.

Note: mean values, gaseous, and only approximate.

mcqs.q: Hess's law states ΔH depends only on:
Bond enthalpies refer to bonds broken in which state?
When you reverse a reaction in a Hess cycle, what happens to ΔH?
options: ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
ΔH stays the same because it's the same reaction.
Its sign reverses — if the forward reaction is +100 kJ/mol, the reverse is -100 kJ/mol.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
